dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Dear friend, remember to nourish your soul at every moment. Ah, and if necessary, you may also fill your pack.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you sell here?

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Please, look this way. My goods are yours to choose from.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How does one nourish the soul...?

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: There are many ways. Reading, for instance, or listening to music... Or simply contemplating in silence, holding a calm conversation with oneself...

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: But I should mention that, in my view, "squandering money" and "chasing after wealth" are most certainly not among them.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Excessive luxury will not bring satisfaction to the soul. On the contrary, once the indulgence has passed, our souls are instead filled with emptiness.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: As for chasing after wealth... Hahahahaha. A purse that bulges too much can sometimes crowd out the soul, leaving no room for one's true self.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Take our dear Knyazev, for example. His life was once completely consumed by both of these things. And now... heh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Farewell. I wish you a pleasant day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, you know him?

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: I met him a few times at banquets long ago. Back then, he was full of drive, proud and confident, as though he were about to ascend to the throne of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: And now, he is disheartened and dejected, as though he has been cast aside like an old shoe...

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: But who can say whether a falcon that has fallen to the depths might not catch the wind once more and soar back into the sky?

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Knyazev's father entrusted him to my care, and instructed me that when his son finds his courage again, I'm to become his teacher and show him how to contend with the cunning serpents in the world of business.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: But, my friend... my young Knyazev. I do not wish to see your empty heart wholly occupied by petty calculations of profit and loss. Before that happens, it should have room for far more beautiful things.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well... what are you planning to teach him?

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: For now, I don't intend to teach him anything. In a few days, I plan to give him several books. Not the grand treatises on commerce he most wishes to read and imitate, of course, but a few novels.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: In those novels, there are those who willingly set foot upon a misguided path, those who cross blades with their own brothers, and those who pity all mankind, only to discover in the end that there is no one who can save them...

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: Dear Knyazev, young Knyazev. Look upon them, and then go in search of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Zheleznov
dialogues.text: ...Believe me. The most important thing in one's life is to find their true self.
